# ScheduledClicker

ScheduledClicker is a free, open-source Windows 11 and macOS desktop utility for scheduling one mouse click at a fixed screen coordinate. It supports an exact future date and time or a monotonic delay, plus single and double click modes.

Official project: https://github.com/HaNa-486/ScheduledClicker
Website: https://hana-486.github.io/ScheduledClicker/
Latest release: https://github.com/HaNa-486/ScheduledClicker/releases/latest
License: MIT
Version: 1.1.2
Operating systems: Windows 11; macOS 13 Ventura or later
Runtimes: Windows .NET Framework 4.x; Apple Swift/AppKit/ApplicationServices

## Verified properties

- Core automated tests: 10/10 Windows tests and 21/21 macOS tests passed.
- User reported both exact-time and delay modes successful on Windows 11.
- The universal Apple silicon + Intel app compiled, passed its test/self-check suite, and passed ad-hoc signature verification on a GitHub-hosted macOS 15 runner. Interactive clicking still requires user-granted Accessibility permission and a physical logged-in desktop.
- Version 1.1.1 fixes macOS Dark Mode readability; version 1.1.2 makes all three displayed millisecond digits update naturally and adds a clock-animation smoke test.
- A user verified exact-time and delay scheduling plus the improved Dark appearance on a MacBook Air.
- No third-party runtime packages, network access, telemetry, accounts, or persistence.
- Microsoft Defender scan found no threats in the published v1.0.0 executable.
- The Windows executable is unsigned; the macOS app is ad-hoc signed but not Apple-notarized.

## Codex use case

ScheduledClicker can press Send on a prepared Codex message after the usage reset time shown by Codex. It does not detect, bypass, reset, or increase any ChatGPT or Codex limit.

## Safety boundary

The tool clicks a fixed coordinate. If a window moves or content changes, it may click the wrong target. Test a harmless target first and avoid unattended payments, deletion, publishing, or irreversible actions.
